decisions.full_context:
`get` copies a named file to the PC. Its optional output-file argument gives
the destination. A named destination is overwritten if it already exists, so
use a new path for a recovered copy. Without that argument the bytes go to
standard output. Binary extraction includes every recorded 128-byte record,
including padding in the last one. With `--text`, extraction stops before the
first `^Z` and converts carriage-return/line-feed pairs to line feeds. A lone
carriage return is retained. Without `^Z`, all recorded bytes undergo that
conversion, including any padding.

decisions.full_context:
The container occupies 20,480 blocks or 10 MiB. SYSTEM begins at block
2,048, 1 MiB into the card, and occupies 1 MiB. WORK starts at block 4,096
and occupies 8 MiB. The default alignment puts each volume on a multiple of

the space before SYSTEM contains only the header and unused padding.

decisions.full_context:
CP/M reads and writes 128-byte records. Four records fit a 512-byte card
block. Space is allocated to files in larger allocation blocks, so a file
with any data occupies at least 2 KiB on G1M or 4 KiB on G8M. The one-record
`STARTUP.CMD` therefore occupies 4 KiB on WORK even though its recorded
length is only 128 bytes.

decisions.full_context:
Registers hold the values passed to a call. `A`, `B`, `C` and `E` each
hold a byte. `BC`, `DE` and `HL` are 16-bit register pairs, large enough
for a memory address. To select a BDOS operation, you put its function number in `C` and
call `0005h`. A byte parameter goes in `E`, while an address or word
parameter goes in `DE`. A byte result is returned in `A` and a word result
in `HL`. For example, function 2 takes the character in `E` and function 9
takes an address in `DE`. In source, `BDOS EQU $0005` gives that call
address a name.
manual_classification_hints: inline code retained in context, excluded from matching
decisions.review_disposition: Byte parameters in E and address/word parameters in DE are explicit parallel alternatives. While supplies their contrast without the comma; all register names and examples remain untouched.

decisions.full_context:
The CCP also supplies a return address when it starts your program. It puts
`0000h` on the inherited stack before jumping to `0100h`. A top-level `RET`
therefore ends the program through the warm-boot jump at `0000h`. Calls
within the program must return before that last `RET`, so it reaches the
word supplied by the CCP.
manual_classification_hints: inline code retained in context, excluded from matching
decisions.review_disposition: Returning from internal calls before the final RET directly explains reaching the CCP-supplied word. The result clause stays clear without the comma and does not alter the inherited-stack contract.

For a program taking one file name, this default FCB supplies the name

decisions.full_context:
The sequential position is split between an *extent*, a group of 128
records, and the record within it. `EX` and `S2` identify the extent.
`CR` selects its next record, normally 0 to 127. At the boundary the BDOS
moves to the next extent as needed. You keep the complete FCB between
calls so those updates and its allocation map remain available.
Appendix A gives the full field contracts and random-record operations.

decisions.review_disposition: This comma closes the apposition a group of 128 records, opened after extent. Retain both boundaries so and the record within it remains the second part of the sequential position rather than part of the extent definition.

decisions.full_context:
The FCB holds file state, while the bytes being read or written go through
a separate memory buffer. The BDOS calls this the *DMA address*. It is a
transfer address in your memory, not a request to program a hardware DMA
controller. Initially it is `0080h`, with room for one 128-byte record.
Function 26 changes it to the address supplied in `DE`.
manual_classification_hints: inline code retained in context, excluded from matching
decisions.review_disposition: The FCB and data-buffer subjects are explicit and while distinguishes their roles. Removing the comma leaves file state versus transferred bytes clear without changing DMA terminology.

decisions.full_context:
SHOW only reads, so it leaves no changed file state to close. A program that
writes must close its updated FCB before finishing. Warm boot flushes pending
writes from the block cache but cannot close the program's FCBs. The write
sequence after SHOW explains how to finish both operations and check them.
decisions.review_disposition: SHOW only reading directly explains why it has no changed file state to close. The comma is optional; the following requirement to close a writing program’s updated FCB remains explicit.

decisions.full_context:
Writing uses an FCB and a DMA buffer in the same way, but the state
must reach the directory before the program finishes. For a new file,
prepare all 36 FCB bytes: the drive, the space-padded name/type and zeroed
state. Choose a name that is not already present. Function 22, make file,
creates a directory entry. It is not a replace-file command.
decisions.review_disposition: The but clause contrasts shared FCB/buffer mechanics with the additional directory-update requirement. Its explicit subject makes the connection clear without a comma. The paired commas around make file are in a later sentence and remain intact.

decisions.full_context:
Page zero occupies `0000h–00FFh` and contains the CP/M jumps and buffers. The
*transient program area*, or TPA, begins at `0100h`. Its upper bound is the
address stored in the jump at `0005h`, read as a word at `0006h`. That address
is the first byte outside the TPA. Your final usable byte is one below it.

decisions.review_disposition: The comma before or opens the alternative name or TPA and the comma after TPA closes it. Retain the pair to mark TPA as the abbreviation of transient program area, with begins at 0100h applying to that same region.

can remain A throughout that run.
